- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

## 8003ef61-23f6-4927-b3d2-173a9286f9b9

Use web_search first for most factual, current-information, research,
comparison, documentation, and troubleshooting questions.

The web_search results include excerpts intended to be useful for answering
directly. If the excerpts contain enough evidence, answer from them — do not
fetch every search result by default. For broad tasks you can issue multiple
`search_queries` in a single web_search call rather than chaining calls.

Use web_fetch when the user asks about a specific URL or page, needs exact
wording or quotes, requests full-page analysis, or when search excerpts are
conflicting or clearly insufficient.



Use web_fetch only when web_search excerpts are not enough: the user asked
about a specific URL or page, you need exact wording or quotes, you need
full-page analysis, or the excerpts are conflicting or clearly insufficient.
Do not fetch every search result by default — search excerpts are usually
answer-ready.

When you do fetch, you can pass multiple related URLs in one call along with
a common `objective`; the tool will return the parts most relevant to it.

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

# 🚀 ANTARYA (अंतर्या) — Dukan Ka Dimaag
### *The Ultimate 3-Brain AI Ecosystem & Two-Stage Hurdle Predictive Command Center for India's 40M+ Kirana Stores & MSMEs*

---

## 🌟 1. Executive Summary & The 1-Minute Pitch

> *"Traditional retail software stores transactions. **ANTARYA stores knowledge.** We have built the first **Self-Learning Predictive Decision Platform & Autonomous AI CEO for Indian Kirana stores and MSMEs**."*

Small retail shopkeepers (**Kirana Dukan owners**) across India form the backbone of the economy, yet they suffer daily from the **Kirana Trilemma**:
1. **Inventory Blindness & Stockouts**: Relying on rough gut feeling leads to either empty shelves on fast-moving items (loss of revenue) or capital locked in dead stock.
2. **Unrecovered Udhaar (Credit/Khata)**: Managing customer debt across physical paper diaries causes forgotten balances and bad debt.
3. **Complex Enterprise Software Friction**: Standard ERPs and accounting tools require formal training, complex categorization, and tedious typing, making them incompatible with the fast, chaotic environment of an active Kirana shop.

**ANTARYA** bridges this digital divide by wrapping **Enterprise-Grade Two-Stage Hurdle Machine Learning** and **Game-Theoretic SHAP Explainability** inside a conversational, voice-driven **Hinglish AI Assistant (`Dukan Ka Dimaag`)**. It converts spoken regional dialects into instant bills, reads wholesale supplier receipts via Computer Vision OCR, predicts item-level stockouts before they happen, and explains every business recommendation in plain, friendly language that shopkeepers understand and trust.

---

## 🧠 2. The 3-Brain Multi-AI Architecture

ANTARYA does not rely on a single generic API wrapper. Instead, it deploys a **3-Brain Tri-Engine Architecture** where three distinct AI specializations operate in harmony over real-time database synchronization:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        ANTARYA CORE API GATEWAY (Node.js)                         |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
           |                             |                             |
           v                             v                             v
+-------------------------+   +-------------------------+   +-------------------------+
|   BRAIN 1: GEMINI 2.5   |   |   BRAIN 2: MEITY BHASH  |   |   BRAIN 3: TWO-STAGE    |
|      (Google GenAI)     |   |      (Government AI)    |   |    (Python FastAPI)     |
+-------------------------+   +-------------------------+   +-------------------------+
| • Multi-Agent Advisory  |   | • Voice POS (ASR)       |   | • Stage 1: CatBoost     |
|   (Finance, Marketing,  |   | • Hands-free regional   |   |   Hurdle Classifier     |
|   Operations Manager)   |   |   dialect billing       |   | • Stage 2: LightGBM     |
| • Vision OCR Invoice &  |   |   (Hindi, Marathi,      |   |   Volume Regressor      |
|   Wholesale Scanner     |   |   Telugu, Tamil, etc.)  |   | • SHAP Shapley Game-    |
| • Live Hinglish Context |   | • Real-time UI dialect  |   |   Theoretic Explainer   |
|   Injected from MongoDB |   |   Translation           |   | • Indian Weather & Ag-  |
|                         |   |                         |   |   marknet Ingestion     |
+-------------------------+   +-------------------------+   +-------------------------+
```

### 🧠 Brain 1: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (`server/routes/ai.js`)
* **Role**: High-level reasoning, conversational Hinglish guidance, and multimodal vision processing.
* **Live Context Injection**: Before answering every query, the backend dynamically builds a real-time shop briefing (`buildShopContext`) reading actual inventory levels, daily sales volume, pending *Udhaar*, and expense ledger directly from MongoDB.
* **Multi-Agent Advisory Board**:
  * 📈 **Finance Minister**: Monitors daily margin, tracks top customer debt accounts (`Khata`), and designs personalized collection strategies.
  * 📣 **Marketing Guru**: Scans customer histories for inactive buyers (14+ days absence) and cross-references them with high-margin items to auto-generate localized WhatsApp re-engagement campaigns.
  * 📦 **Operations Manager**: Identifies zero-turnover dead stock and flags urgent low-stock items for immediate distributor reordering.
* **📸 Multimodal Vision Bill Scanner (`/api/ai/scan-bill`)**: Lets shopkeepers snap a photo of unstructured physical wholesale receipts. Google Gemini Vision extracts exact item names, unit purchase prices, and quantities, automatically populating the store's digital inventory.

### 🧠 Brain 2: MeitY Bhashini AI Platform (`server/routes/ai.js`)
* **Role**: Government of India national AI speech platform delivering ultra-low latency Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) tailored specifically for Indian accents and regional trade vocabulary.
* **Hands-Free Voice POS (`Bol Kar Bill Banayein`)**: Allows shopkeepers to speak naturally (`"Do packet Amul butter, teen litre doodh, aur ek kilo cheeni add karo"`). The system instantly transcribes the audio, parses product SKUs against the live database, calculates line totals, and settles checkout in seconds.

### 🧠 Brain 3: Two-Stage Hurdle Machine Learning Engine (`ml-service/main.py`)
* **Role**: Autonomous demand forecasting, stockout probability scoring, and executive CEO daily briefing generation (`port 8000`).
* **Why Two-Stage Hurdle? (Solving the Intermittency Paradox)**:
  In Indian Kirana stores, **76.0% of products exhibit lumpy, intermittent demand (>50% zero-sale days)**. Forcing standard single-stage GBDT regression models (like XGBoost or basic CatBoost) to predict daily point forecasts causes massive WMAPE inflation and spits out annoying fractional noise (`0.14 packets of Vim Bar per day`), which shopkeepers immediately reject.
* **How ANTARYA v7 Hurdle Architecture Works**:
  1. **Stage 1 (CatBoost Purchase Occurrence Classifier)**: Evaluates Indian calendar features (`Day of Week`, `Month`, `Payday Proximity`, `Festival Countdowns`) and live Indian weather metrics (`Temperature`, `Rainfall`) to classify whether a sale will occur today ($P(\text{demand}) > \tau$). If $P \le \tau$, it outputs `0`, slashing false alarms on zero-demand days by **88.3%**!
  2. **Stage 2 (CatBoost/LightGBM Positive Demand Regressor)**: If demand is classified as likely ($P > \tau$), Stage 2 predicts exact whole-integer SKU sales volume ($E[\text{sales} \mid \text{sales} > 0]$).
  3. **AntaryaExplainer (Exact Tree SHAP Values)**: Computes game-theoretic Shapley values (`/explain`) so every prediction tells the shopkeeper *why* demand shifted (`"Sunday footfall + upcoming payday cycle added +18% demand surge"`).
  4. **Live External Ingestion Pipelines**: Automatically fetches real-time Indian weather data (`fetch_weather.py`) and Government Agmarknet commodity pricing (`import_local_agmarknet.py`) to keep feature vectors fresh.

---

## 💻 3. Complete Production Feature Catalog (`client/src/screens/`)

Every single feature below is **100% real-data synchronized** with MongoDB and Python FastAPI (`v7.0.0-hurdle`). All simulated demo fallbacks have been permanently removed.

### 1. ⚡ SaaS Command Center Dashboard (`Dashboard.jsx`)
* **12-Column Symmetrical Bento Grid (`1266x643` & Mobile Viewports)**: Perfectly balanced left/right layout featuring glassmorphic cards and zero right-heavy visual bias.
* **🟢 Two-Stage AI Model Synchronized Badge**: Real-time heartbeat indicator confirming active WebSocket/REST connection to the Python Hurdle ML microservice (`localhost:8000`).
* **Aaj Ki AI Salah (Urgent Advice Card)**: Live high-priority alert powered by Hurdle predictions (e.g., *"Fortune Sunflower Oil 1L ka stock khatam ho sakta hai! Abhi aapke pass sirf 8 unit bache hain."*).
* **Direct WhatsApp Order Generator**: One-click green CTA that formats a professional, instant restocking purchase order for the store's wholesale distributor (`WhatsApp Se Turant Order Karein`).
* **Live Financial KPIs**: Real-time aggregation of *Aaj Ki Kamai* (Today's Revenue), *Aaj Ke Bills* (Completed Transactions), and *Total Saaman* (Active SKU Count & Stockout Warnings).
* **Pichle 7 Din Ki Kamai (Interactive Sales Chart)**: CSS-rendered responsive bar chart displaying daily cash vs. UPI revenue breakdown across the week.
* **Turant Kaam (Quick Action Matrix)**: Fast navigation grid to create voice bills (`Bol Kar Banayein`), add inventory (`Naya Saaman Jodein`), consult the AI advisor (`AI Se Salah Lein`), or manage customer credit (`Khata & Udhaari`).
* **Aaj Ke Turant Bills (Live Transaction Feed)**: Real-time ticker showing the latest customer sales, timestamps, payment methods (`Cash / UPI`), and verification checkmarks.

### 2. 🧠 Dukaan Dimaag — Store Intelligence Engine (`LearningEngine.jsx`)
* **100% Real Database Analytics**: Displays actual live counts directly from MongoDB (`450+ Bills Analyzed`, `39+ Days of Learning`, `450+ Recommendations Made so far`).
* **What ANTARYA Knows About Your Shop**: Autonomous feature extraction showing discovered *Busiest Hours (`7–9 AM, 6–9 PM`)*, *Most Popular Product (`Milk — 32 sold/day avg`)*, and *Fastest Growing Category (`Curd +40% this week`)*.
* **Money Saved Calculator**: Real-time computation of rupees saved (`₹1,240+`) by preventing stockouts and reducing perishable dairy wastage.
* **Business Health Star Rating & Risk Indicator**: Dynamic star rating (`★★★★☆ Good/Excellent`) and real-time operational risk status (`🟢 Low Risk Today`).

### 3. 🎙️ Bol Kar Bill — Voice POS & Quick Sale (`QuickSale.jsx`)
* **Hands-Free Regional Voice Billing**: Powered by **MeitY Bhashini ASR pipeline (`64392f96daac500b55c543cd`)**, enabling effortless Hindi/Regional billing (`"Do packet Amul butter aur ek kilo sugar add karo"`).
* **Automatic Item Parsing & Cart Calculation**: Instantly matches spoken phrases against database SKUs, adds exact quantities, applies selling prices, and calculates cart totals.
* **Dual Payment Settlement**: One-click instant checkout supporting both **Cash** and **UPI / QR Code** transactions with instant MongoDB receipt persistence.

README
MUTAGENT
MUTAGENT
The Agentic Development Lifecycle — build · evaluate · diagnose · optimize AI agents, all from one conversational orchestrator.
hackathon Helix ADL stages any harness
🏆 The Hackathon Challenge
Build the most sophisticated AI agent you can — with Mutagent — and max out the system. Spec it, build it in any harness or framework (Mastra · LangGraph · Claude Code · Codex · …), and drive it through the full lifecycle. The more capable and ambitious the agent — real jobs, tools, integrations, triggers — the better.
Then push the system itself: close the loop so your agent self-evolves, and — for bonus glory — extend the base system with your own stage, *command, or skill.
How you win (pick your angle — the strongest submissions hit several)
Most sophisticated agent (headline) — how far you max out the system: ambition & complexity, real jobs, tools, triggers, integrations.
Self-evolving loop — run the system as a closed, self-improving loop: *build → *evaluate → *diagnose → *optimize, on repeat.
🏆 Greatest extension to the base system (bonus) — add a new ADL stage / *command / skill that cleanly fits Helix.
Proof it works — real eval criteria + a dataset (≥ 20 items) + a passing scorecard.
Best product feedback — the sharpest, most actionable feedback on the system, filed with mutagent-cli feedback.
What you deliver
Agent code — on this repo, under submissions/<your-team>/ (via PR).
Session transcripts — the main session and every subagent it spawned. Required.
All traces — every run your agent produced, exported and included with your submission. Required.
Product feedback — filed via mutagent-cli feedback "..." as you go.
📖 Full walkthrough: quickstart.html (open in a browser) · printable deck: quickstart.pdf · full docs: docs.mutagent.io.
What is MutagenT?
MutagenT drives a skill or agent through the Agentic Development Lifecycle (ADL) — a loop you steer in plain language. You describe an agent and it gets spec'd, built, evaluated, diagnosed, and improved, with you in control at every gate. One orchestrator (Helix) routes each stage to a specialized subagent; nothing auto-advances, and every apply is approval-gated.
① SPEC ──▶ ② BUILD ──▶ ③ EVALUATE ──▶ ④ DIAGNOSE ──▶ ⑤ OPTIMIZE ──┐ ↺
   ▲────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   enter at any stage · transitions are explicit · the EDD inner loop runs until the gate passes
The Agentic Development Lifecycle — sequenced by the Helix orchestrator
Key Features
One orchestrator, many subagents — Helix sequences spec → build → evaluate → diagnose → optimize and routes each stage to its owning skill. It conducts; it never does the stage's inner work.
Spec → impl, one direction — a guided interview emits a portable agentspec.yaml; *build implements it into your chosen target and a reviewer checks the result actually matches the spec.
Eval-driven development — mine criteria, build a dataset, and judge real runs into a binary pass/fail scorecard; failures route to diagnosis. The judge only judges — it never silently fixes.
Two eval substrates — a built-in host-runtime judge (no provider key), or an exported code eval suite (deterministic checks + LLM-as-judge) that runs in your own stack/CI.
Diagnose → optimize, gated — root-cause with ranked fixes; an AI engineer applies the chosen one and re-evaluates, looping until green. Nothing changes without your go-ahead.
Any harness — Mastra, LangGraph, or coding-agent harnesses like Claude Code / Codex.
Conversational + explicit — type a *command, or just say what you want. Free text routes; gates hold.
Quick Start
# 1 · fork this repo on GitHub, then clone your fork
git clone https://github.com/<your-team>/mutagent-hackathon && cd mutagent-hackathon
# 2 · install the system  (CLI → sign in → agents + skills into .claude/ and .codex/)
npm install -g @mutagent/cli     # or pnpm / bun
mutagent login
mutagent install helix
# 3 · boot your coding agent, then summon the orchestrator
claude                           # or codex
> *mutagent                      # or /mutagent-helix
📖 New here? Open the walkthrough quickstart.html (or quickstart.pdf); full docs at docs.mutagent.io.
mutagent boots Helix — the ADL dashboard, the system map, and the command roster:
🧬  MUTAGENT · ADL Orchestrator — Helix routes to your subagents
  LIFECYCLE   ① SPEC → ② BUILD → ③ EVALUATE → ④ DIAGNOSE → ⑤ OPTIMIZE
  SYSTEM      agentspec · builder · evaluator · diagnostics · optimize
  SETUP       ⚠ not onboarded yet — run *onboard
  COMMANDS    *spec  *build  *evaluate  *diagnose  *optimize  *onboard  *status
The Commands
Command	Stage	What it does	You get
*onboard	setup	add provider keys · workspace · models	a config
*spec	①	guided interview → a portable spec	agentspec.yaml
*build	②	implement the spec into your target + verify	a working agent + report
*evaluate	③	judge real runs → pass/fail per behavior	a scorecard
*diagnose	④	root-cause the failures → ranked fixes	a diagnosis report
*optimize	⑤	apply the fix, re-evaluate — gated, looping until green	updated agent + fresh scorecard
Don't know the name? Just say it: "design a new agent that triages our support inbox", "evaluate the agent on its last 50 runs", "why did it fail its escalation eval?" — Helix routes it.
Repo Layout
mutagent-hackathon/
├── README.md              ← you are here
├── quickstart.html        ← the full walkthrough (open in a browser)
├── quickstart.pdf         ← printable, branded deck
└── submissions/<team>/    ← your challenge goes here (via PR)
The Mutagent system itself (agents + skills) is installed locally via mutagent install helix, not committed here.
🧩 Submitting your challenge
Submissions are by pull request — the standard fork-and-PR flow:
Fork this repo.
Add your work under submissions/<your-team>/ — your agent, its agentspec.yaml, the eval suite, and a short README.md (what it does, how to run it, your eval results).
Include your session transcripts — the main session AND every subagent it spawned — so judges can replay the full build & eval (agentic runs fan out to sub-agents; we want those too). Put them under submissions/<your-team>/transcripts/:
Claude Code — all the run's .jsonl from ~/.claude/projects/<your-project-folder>/ (the main session plus any sub-agent sessions it produced)
Codex — every rollout-*.jsonl under ~/.codex/sessions/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/ for your run — the main session and each sub-agent are separate rollout files (archived runs under ~/.codex/archived_sessions/)
Include all your traces — every run your agent produced (the top-level traces/ dir is git-ignored, so copy them into submissions/<your-team>/traces/ so they ship with your PR).
File product feedback with mutagent-cli feedback "..." as you build — the sharpest, most actionable feedback is its own judging track.
Open a pull request to main — a maintainer reviews and merges (direct pushes to main are disabled).
One self-contained PR per submission, scoped to your submissions/<your-team>/ folder.

🚀 ANTARYA (अंतर्या) — Dukan Ka Dimaag
The Ultimate 3-Brain AI Ecosystem & Two-Stage Hurdle Predictive Command Center for India's 40M+ Kirana Stores & MSMEs
Status: Production-Ready Frontend: React + Vite Backend: Node + Express Database: MongoDB Atlas + MemoryDB ML Engine: Python + FastAPI Brain 1: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Brain 2: MeitY Bhashini AI
🌟 1. Executive Summary & The 1-Minute Pitch
"Traditional retail software stores transactions. ANTARYA stores knowledge. We have built the first Self-Learning Predictive Decision Platform & Autonomous AI CEO for Indian Kirana stores and MSMEs."
Small retail shopkeepers (Kirana Dukan owners) across India form the backbone of the economy, yet they suffer daily from the Kirana Trilemma:
Inventory Blindness & Stockouts: Relying on rough gut feeling leads to either empty shelves on fast-moving items (loss of revenue) or capital locked in dead stock.
Unrecovered Udhaar (Credit/Khata): Managing customer debt across physical paper diaries causes forgotten balances and bad debt.
Complex Enterprise Software Friction: Standard ERPs and accounting tools require formal training, complex categorization, and tedious typing, making them incompatible with the fast, chaotic environment of an active Kirana shop.
ANTARYA bridges this digital divide by wrapping Enterprise-Grade Two-Stage Hurdle Machine Learning and Game-Theoretic SHAP Explainability inside a conversational, voice-driven Hinglish AI Assistant (Dukan Ka Dimaag). It converts spoken regional dialects into instant bills, reads wholesale supplier receipts via Computer Vision OCR, predicts item-level stockouts before they happen, and explains every business recommendation in plain, friendly language that shopkeepers understand and trust.

🧠 Brain 3: Two-Stage Hurdle Machine Learning Engine (ml-service/main.py)
Role: Autonomous demand forecasting, stockout probability scoring, and executive CEO daily briefing generation (port 8000).

MUTAGENT
MUTAGENT
The Agentic Development Lifecycle — build · evaluate · diagnose · optimize AI agents, all from one conversational orchestrator.
hackathon Helix ADL stages any harness
🏆 The Hackathon Challenge
Build the most sophisticated AI agent you can — with Mutagent — and max out the system. Spec it, build it in any harness or framework (Mastra · LangGraph · Claude Code · Codex · …), and drive it through the full lifecycle. The more capable and ambitious the agent — real jobs, tools, integrations, triggers — the better.
Then push the system itself: close the loop so your agent self-evolves, and — for bonus glory — extend the base system with your own stage, *command, or skill.
How you win (pick your angle — the strongest submissions hit several)
Most sophisticated agent (headline) — how far you max out the system: ambition & complexity, real jobs, tools, triggers, integrations.
Self-evolving loop — run the system as a closed, self-improving loop: *build → *evaluate → *diagnose → *optimize, on repeat.
🏆 Greatest extension to the base system (bonus) — add a new ADL stage / *command / skill that cleanly fits Helix.
Proof it works — real eval criteria + a dataset (≥ 20 items) + a passing scorecard.
Best product feedback — the sharpest, most actionable feedback on the system, filed with mutagent-cli feedback.
What you deliver
Agent code — on this repo, under submissions/<your-team>/ (via PR).
Session transcripts — the main session and every subagent it spawned. Required.
All traces — every run your agent produced, exported and included with your submission. Required.
Product feedback — filed via mutagent-cli feedback "..." as you go.
📖 Full walkthrough: quickstart.html (open in a browser) · printable deck: quickstart.pdf · full docs: docs.mutagent.io.
What is MutagenT?
MutagenT drives a skill or agent through the Agentic Development Lifecycle (ADL) — a loop you steer in plain language. You describe an agent and it gets spec'd, built, evaluated, diagnosed, and improved, with you in control at every gate. One orchestrator (Helix) routes each stage to a specialized subagent; nothing auto-advances, and every apply is approval-gated.
① SPEC ──▶ ② BUILD ──▶ ③ EVALUATE ──▶ ④ DIAGNOSE ──▶ ⑤ OPTIMIZE ──┐ ↺
   ▲────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   enter at any stage · transitions are explicit · the EDD inner loop runs until the gate passes
The Agentic Development Lifecycle — sequenced by the Helix orchestrator
Key Features
One orchestrator, many subagents — Helix sequences spec → build → evaluate → diagnose → optimize and routes each stage to its owning skill. It conducts; it never does the stage's inner work.
Spec → impl, one direction — a guided interview emits a portable agentspec.yaml; *build implements it into your chosen target and a reviewer checks the result actually matches the spec.
Eval-driven development — mine criteria, build a dataset, and judge real runs into a binary pass/fail scorecard; failures route to diagnosis. The judge only judges — it never silently fixes.
Two eval substrates — a built-in host-runtime judge (no provider key), or an exported code eval suite (deterministic checks + LLM-as-judge) that runs in your own stack/CI.
Diagnose → optimize, gated — root-cause with ranked fixes; an AI engineer applies the chosen one and re-evaluates, looping until green. Nothing changes without your go-ahead.
Any harness — Mastra, LangGraph, or coding-agent harnesses like Claude Code / Codex.
Conversational + explicit — type a *command, or just say what you want. Free text routes; gates hold.
Quick Start
# 1 · fork this repo on GitHub, then clone your fork
git clone https://github.com/<your-team>/mutagent-hackathon && cd mutagent-hackathon
# 2 · install the system  (CLI → sign in → agents + skills into .claude/ and .codex/)
npm install -g @mutagent/cli     # or pnpm / bun
mutagent login
mutagent install helix
# 3 · boot your coding agent, then summon the orchestrator
claude                           # or codex
> *mutagent                      # or /mutagent-helix
📖 New here? Open the walkthrough quickstart.html (or quickstart.pdf); full docs at docs.mutagent.io.
mutagent boots Helix — the ADL dashboard, the system map, and the command roster:
🧬  MUTAGENT · ADL Orchestrator — Helix routes to your subagents
  LIFECYCLE   ① SPEC → ② BUILD → ③ EVALUATE → ④ DIAGNOSE → ⑤ OPTIMIZE
  SYSTEM      agentspec · builder · evaluator · diagnostics · optimize
  SETUP       ⚠ not onboarded yet — run *onboard
  COMMANDS    *spec  *build  *evaluate  *diagnose  *optimize  *onboard  *status
The Commands
Command	Stage	What it does	You get
*onboard	setup	add provider keys · workspace · models	a config
*spec	①	guided interview → a portable spec	agentspec.yaml
*build	②	implement the spec into your target + verify	a working agent + report
*evaluate	③	judge real runs → pass/fail per behavior	a scorecard
*diagnose	④	root-cause the failures → ranked fixes	a diagnosis report
*optimize	⑤	apply the fix, re-evaluate — gated, looping until green	updated agent + fresh scorecard
Don't know the name? Just say it: "design a new agent that triages our support inbox", "evaluate the agent on its last 50 runs", "why did it fail its escalation eval?" — Helix routes it.

The Ultimate 3-Brain AI Ecosystem & Two-Stage Hurdle Predictive Command Center for India's 40M+ Kirana Stores & MSMEs
Status: Production-Ready Frontend: React + Vite Backend: Node + Express Database: MongoDB Atlas + MemoryDB ML Engine: Python + FastAPI Brain 1: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Brain 2: MeitY Bhashini AI
🌟 1. Executive Summary & The 1-Minute Pitch
"Traditional retail software stores transactions. ANTARYA stores knowledge. We have built the first Self-Learning Predictive Decision Platform & Autonomous AI CEO for Indian Kirana stores and MSMEs."
Small retail shopkeepers (Kirana Dukan owners) across India form the backbone of the economy, yet they suffer daily from the Kirana Trilemma:
Inventory Blindness & Stockouts: Relying on rough gut feeling leads to either empty shelves on fast-moving items (loss of revenue) or capital locked in dead stock.
Unrecovered Udhaar (Credit/Khata): Managing customer debt across physical paper diaries causes forgotten balances and bad debt.
Complex Enterprise Software Friction: Standard ERPs and accounting tools require formal training, complex categorization, and tedious typing, making them incompatible with the fast, chaotic environment of an active Kirana shop.
ANTARYA bridges this digital divide by wrapping Enterprise-Grade Two-Stage Hurdle Machine Learning and Game-Theoretic SHAP Explainability inside a conversational, voice-driven Hinglish AI Assistant (Dukan Ka Dimaag). It converts spoken regional dialects into instant bills, reads wholesale supplier receipts via Computer Vision OCR, predicts item-level stockouts before they happen, and explains every business recommendation in plain, friendly language that shopkeepers understand and trust.

Worse, recommending that a shopkeeper order "0.14 packets of Vim Bar today and 0.22 packets tomorrow" causes extreme operational annoyance, since distributors deliver in Whole-Integer Cartons / Petis on weekly cycles.
Empirical Proof: ANTARYA v7 (Two-Stage Hurdle) vs. v6 (Single-Stage)
To solve this, we developed ANTARYA v7 (train_v7.py), combining a Purchase Occurrence Classifier ($P(\text{sales} > 0)$) with a Conditional Positive Regressor (
E
[
sales
∣
sales
>
0
]
) and a 7-Day Weekly Batch Aggregation Engine.
On a strict 15,500 hold-out test set, ANTARYA v7 proved superior:
Evaluation Metric	ANTARYA v6 (Single-Stage GBDT)	ANTARYA v7 (Two-Stage Hurdle)	Engineering Impact & Business Breakthrough
Daily WMAPE (%)	76.63%	71.27%	-5.36% error reduction across all store items
Daily MAE (units)	0.9573 units	0.8905 units	+7.0% precision gain per day
False-Positive Noise on Zero Days	70.90%	8.30%	88.3% drop in daily false-alarm recommendations!
Intermittent Goods WMAPE (>40% zeros)	106.16%	89.52%	-16.64% WMAPE reduction! Stops predicting fractional daily noise on dormant items.
Weekly Batch Distributor Reorder WMAPE	36.22%	36.22% / 42.87%	Outputs exact whole-carton distributor order recommendations for 7-day batch cycles (MAE ~2.8 units/week).
Solving the Day-1 Cold-Start Problem
When a new Kirana store signs up, ANTARYA solves the zero-data cold-start problem immediately using our global Foundation Model (indian_v7_hurdle_model.pkl) trained across 395,000 retail days. As the shopkeeper records transactions over the first 30 to 90 days, the Learning Engine (/api/learning) tracks Prediction Error (Predicted vs. Actual), detects demand drift, and automatically blends the global foundation weights with local store-specific feature vectors—creating an autonomous AI brain 100% customized to that exact neighborhood!
🔌 6. Complete Backend REST API Catalog (server/routes/)
The Node.js + Express API Gateway (port 5001) handles stateless authentication, data persistence, and routing:
Route Prefix	Controller File (server/routes/)	Key Endpoints & Core Capabilities
/api/auth	auth.js	POST /register, POST /login, GET /me, POST /complete-setup — Secure JWT authentication and Kirana store onboarding.
/api/products	products.js	GET /, POST /, PUT /:id, DELETE /:id, POST /bulk-update, POST /seed-demo — Full inventory management and stockout thresholds.
/api/sales	sales.js	POST /, GET /today, GET /summary, GET /history — High-speed POS billing logging (Cash/UPI), revenue computation, and ledger adjustments.
/api/customers	customers.js	GET /, POST /, POST /:id/pay-credit — Digital Khata CRM tracking lifetime spending and partial/full Udhaar credit repayments.
/api/dashboard	dashboard.js	GET /kpi, GET /suggestions, GET /charts, POST /expense — Live 360° revenue aggregation, urgent AI advice cards, and overhead expense logging.
/api/complaints	complaints.js	GET /, POST /, PUT /:id/resolve — Customer issue tracking register with AI-generated polite resolution suggestions.
/api/learning	learning.js	GET /evolution, GET /accuracy-trends, POST /log-prediction — Real-time analytics exposing actual DB counts (450+ bills, 39+ days).
/api/ml	ml.js	Proxy bridge passing DB inventory to Python FastAPI (/predict, /explain, /ceo-brief, /retrain).
/api/ai	ai.js	POST /advisor, POST /chat, POST /scan-bill, POST /speech-to-text, POST /translate, GET /status — Gemini 2.5 Flash and Bhashini AI routing.
💻 7. Setup & Installation Guide
Prerequisites
Node.js: v18.0.0 or higher
Python: v3.10 or higher (for ml-service)
MongoDB Atlas Account: Optional (system automatically falls back to local memory DB if unavailable)
API Keys: Google Gemini API Key (GEMINI_API_KEY) & MeitY Bhashini credentials (optional, has fallbacks)
Step-by-Step Quick Start
1. Clone the Repository
git clone https://github.com/Arjundas08/antarya.git
cd antarya
2. Install All Node Dependencies (Root, Server & Client)
npm run install:all
(Or install manually inside each folder: npm install in root, cd server && npm install, cd ../client && npm install).
3. Configure Environment Variables (server/.env)
Create a .env file inside the server/ directory:
PORT=5001
MONGO_URI=your_mongodb_atlas_connection_string
GEMINI_API_KEY=your_google_gemini_api_key
JWT_SECRET=antarya_super_secret_jwt_key_2026
BHASHINI_API_KEY=your_bhashini_api_key_optional
4. Initialize Python Machine Learning Microservice (ml-service/)
Open a separate terminal window to launch the FastAPI Hurdle Engine:
cd ml-service
python -m venv .venv
# On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate | On Mac/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
(The ML engine will load saved_models/indian_v7_hurdle_model.pkl and expose Swagger API documentation at http://localhost:8000/docs).
5. Launch the Concurrent Ecosystem (Server + Client)
Return to the project root directory and run our concurrent startup command:
npm run dev
Frontend UI: Opens automatically at http://localhost:5173
Express Backend: Listening at http://localhost:5001
Python ML Service: Listening at http://localhost:8000
Note
Upon running npm run dev, if your IP is not whitelisted on MongoDB Atlas or internet connection drops, the terminal may pause for exactly 30 seconds while attempting cloud connection before gracefully spawning the internal mongodb-memory-server and booting successfully!
🗺️ 8. Enterprise Roadmap & Defensibility Moat
What makes ANTARYA defensible against competitors? Data Gravity & Continuous Learning. A competitor can copy a UI layout overnight, but they cannot copy an AI brain that has spent 6 months fine-tuning its weights (/api/learning/evolution) to the exact purchase patterns of a specific neighborhood. The longer a store uses ANTARYA, the smarter its recommendations become, creating absolute vendor lock-in.
Production Roadmap (Post-Hackathon Execution)
Automated Celery/Redis Retraining Workers: Migrate our manual/demo retraining trigger (LearningEngine.jsx) into a background Celery worker queue that runs fine-tuning jobs nightly during store off-hours (2:00 AM).
Direct WhatsApp Bot Notification Agent: Push morning CEO Action Briefings and automated distributor PO PDFs directly to the shopkeeper's WhatsApp number before they open the store.
Multi-Tenant Hopsworks Feature Store: Deploy Hopsworks to compute real-time rolling demand statistics (lag_7, rolling_mean_30d) across thousands of concurrent Kirana tenants with sub-10ms query latency.
Agmarknet & Mandi Live Price Feed Expansion: Scale import_local_agmarknet.py to cover real-time APMC Mandi commodity price indices across all 28 Indian states, warning shopkeepers of impending wholesale price inflation (e.g., onion/potato price surges).
Built with ❤️ for the Indian Merchant Ecosystem. We don't just build software; we build internal strength (Antarya).

# ANTARYA × Mutagent — Autonomous Store Manager Implementation Plan

## Context

HackIndia Spark-11's Mutagent track judges on: (1) most sophisticated agent — real jobs/tools/triggers/integrations, (2) a **closed, self-improving dev loop** (`*build → *evaluate → *diagnose → *optimize`, on repeat), (3) a bonus extension to the ADL system itself, (4) proof via a ≥20-item dataset + passing scorecard, (5) product feedback filed with `mutagent-cli feedback`. Submission requires the PR to `mutagent-io/mutagent-hackathon` under `submissions/team-nirvikalp/`, **plus the actual Claude Code session `.jsonl` transcripts** (main + sub-agents) and all trace files — so the Mutagent ADL work must happen live in Claude Code sessions run from this project, not be written up after the fact.

ANTARYA today has real, working AI modules (Gemini chat/advisor/vision OCR, Bhashini voice, a two-stage hurdle ML service) but they don't coordinate — nothing evaluates whether yesterday's forecast was right, diagnoses why, or improves tomorrow's thresholds. The user's blueprint asks for an "Autonomous Store Manager" that makes Mutagent load-bearing, not decorative.

**Key correction to the user's blueprint**: Mutagent's ADL (`*spec/*build/*evaluate/*diagnose/*optimize`) is a **development-lifecycle tool driven by a coding agent**, not a runtime API you call per HTTP request. The plan below keeps that distinction explicit and makes it the actual selling point:

1. **Runtime layer** (our code) — `Autonomous Store Manager`: a 7-stage orchestration (Observe→Understand→Evaluate→Diagnose→Optimize→Execute→Learn) that runs live when the owner clicks "Start," using ANTARYA's existing Gemini/Bhashini/ML modules as tools. This is the "sophisticated agent, real jobs/tools/triggers" criterion.
2. **Dev-time layer** (Mutagent ADL, run inside Claude Code) — used to *spec, build, evaluate, diagnose, and optimize* the Store Manager's own logic (reorder thresholds, confidence gates, prompts) against a real dataset. This is the "self-evolving loop" criterion.
3. **The connective tissue that makes Mutagent essential, not bolted on** — the Store Manager's LEARN stage writes every decision + its real outcome (predicted vs. actual) into Mongo. That log becomes the **eval dataset** Mutagent judges in `*evaluate`. `*diagnose` explains real failures (not synthetic ones). `*optimize` changes real thresholds/prompts, committed back into the runtime code. Run it twice (baseline cycle → optimize → second cycle) to produce a documented before/after improvement, not a static 100% claim.

This also fixes a currently broken route (`POST /api/ml/predict` proxies to a nonexistent FastAPI `/predict` — only `/predict/demand` and `/predict/stockout` exist) and replaces the fabricated 100% `scorecard.json` with real numbers, per the user's explicit decision.

## Scope decisions (from user)

- **Scorecard**: regenerate honestly from real execution traces. Ship two cycles: baseline pass/fail numbers → diagnose → optimize → second cycle showing measurable improvement on the same dataset. Include business metrics (stockouts prevented, forecast error change, response time, revenue impact) alongside pass/fail.
- **Trigger model**: both — manual "Start Autonomous Store Manager" button for the live demo, plus an optional scheduled early-morning run (`node-cron`) for the "always-on OS" narrative.

## Architecture

### 1. Runtime: Autonomous Store Manager

**New file `server/services/storeManager.js`** — orchestrates the cycle by calling *existing* code, not reimplementing it:

- OBSERVE: reuse `buildShopContext(shopId)` from `server/routes/ai.js` (products/sales/customers/expenses) + `GET /api/dashboard/` KPIs + `GET /api/dashboard/suggestions` + `POST /api/ml/ceo-brief`. Bundle into one structured `StoreContext` object (the current `buildShopContext` returns a prose string for Gemini — add a sibling function returning structured JSON for the orchestrator to reason over programmatically).
- UNDERSTAND: one Gemini call (reuse the model-fallback pattern already in `ai.js`) that turns `StoreContext` into a prioritized list of business problems, not API calls.
- EVALUATE: pull the last cycle's decisions from the new `DecisionTrace` collection, join against `ActualLog` (already tracks `absoluteError`/`percentageError` per `server/routes/learning.js`) to score each prior recommendation pass/fail.
- DIAGNOSE: for each failed prediction, a Gemini call constrained to the specific failure taxonomy in the blueprint (weather, festival, supplier delay, threshold, seasonality) — not generic text.
- OPTIMIZE: propose concrete parameter changes (e.g., adjust `minStock` threshold, safety_stock in the `/ceo-brief` call, confidence cutoff) — stored as a proposal, not silently applied (mirrors Mutagent's own "nothing auto-advances, every apply is approval-gated" principle).
- EXECUTE (only after owner approval or auto-approve toggle): calls existing endpoints — WhatsApp order text generation (already in Dashboard.jsx pattern), `POST /api/learning/log-prediction`, writes a `DecisionTrace` row.
- LEARN: every stage's input/output is appended to `DecisionTrace`; this is what feeds Mutagent's eval dataset later.

**New Mongo schema** in `server/db.js`: `DecisionTrace { shopId, cycleId, stage, input, output, actionTaken, timestamp, outcome, linkedPredictionLogId }`.

**New route `server/routes/storeManager.js`**: `POST /api/store-manager/run` (executes one full cycle, streams stage progress via SSE or polling for the "Observing Shop… Evaluating Yesterday…" UI), `GET /api/store-manager/history` (past cycles/traces), `POST /api/store-manager/approve` (approves a pending OPTIMIZE/EXECUTE proposal). Mount in `server/index.js` alongside existing routers.

**Fix while touching ml.js**: `server/routes/ml.js` `POST /predict` currently forwards to nonexistent FastAPI `/predict` — repoint to `/predict/demand` or `/predict/stockout` based on request shape (or add both as explicit routes) so OBSERVE doesn't fail on day one.

**Scheduled trigger**: add `node-cron` (or reuse if already a dependency — verify) in `server/index.js` to call the same orchestrator function on an early-morning schedule, writing results for the owner to review on login — same code path as the manual button, just a different trigger.

### 2. Frontend: Autonomous Store Manager screen

New `client/src/screens/StoreManager.jsx` (+ CSS, following existing screen patterns like `LearningEngine.jsx`): a "▶ Start Autonomous Store Manager" button that triggers `POST /api/store-manager/run`, then renders the 7-stage progress narrative from the blueprint (🧠 Observing Shop... → ✅ Shop Ready For Today) using stage events from the backend — no Mutagent terminology exposed to the shop owner, per the blueprint's UX principle. Add nav entry alongside existing screens.

### 3. Dev-time: Mutagent ADL loop (run inside Claude Code, produces submission artifacts)

Executed as actual Claude Code sessions from this project directory (required so `.jsonl` transcripts exist for submission):

1. `*spec` — author/refine `submissions/team-nirvikalp/agentspec.yaml` to describe the Autonomous Store Manager specifically (not the whole app) — capabilities: `observe_business_context`, `evaluate_past_decisions`, `diagnose_failure`, `optimize_thresholds`, `execute_actions`, `learn_from_outcomes`.
2. `*build` — have Mutagent's builder implement/verify the storeManager.js module against that spec (this is the actual coding work above, run through the ADL rather than ad hoc).
3. `*evaluate` — run against `submissions/team-nirvikalp/eval_suite.json` (treat as source of truth over the root duplicate `mutagent_eval_suite.json`) **extended** with real cases derived from `DecisionTrace`+`ActualLog` joins, not just hand-authored prompts.
4. `*diagnose` — root-cause real failures from that first evaluate run.
5. `*optimize` — apply the fix (e.g., a threshold or prompt change) — gated, per Mutagent's approval model.
6. Re-run `*evaluate` — second scorecard, same dataset, showing the delta. This before/after pair is the "self-improving loop" proof.
7. File feedback throughout via `mutagent-cli feedback "..."` as real friction is hit (not retrofitted).

Use `Skill(mutagent-cli)` for exact command syntax rather than guessing — it's already installed per `.mutagentrc.json` (workspace `0262ac0d-b8cc-4b0a-a568-148db0bbb597`).

### 4. Submission hygiene (blocking issues, must happen before opening the PR)

- **Secret scrub**: `MUTAGENT_CLAUDE_CODE_BLUEPRINT.md` (committed, public repo, commit `6c1c2bd`) contains a live MongoDB Atlas connection string with username — rotate that Atlas credential and scrub the file before any public PR. Also check `.jsonl` transcripts and `traces/` for embedded env vars/keys before copying them into `submissions/team-nirvikalp/transcripts/` and `submissions/team-nirvikalp/traces/`.
- **Correct target repo**: the PR goes to `mutagent-io/mutagent-hackathon` (fork it), scoped to `submissions/team-nirvikalp/` — not to `Arjundas08/antarya3` as one blueprint draft stated.
- **Scorecard**: replace `submissions/team-nirvikalp/scorecard.json` with the real two-cycle (baseline → optimized) results from step 6 above, plus a short narrative tying it to business metrics (stockout reduction, WMAPE change, response time, revenue impact) — consistent with the blueprint's own Q&A admission of a 45% real pass rate, not contradicting it.
- **Single source of truth**: use `submissions/team-nirvikalp/agentspec.yaml` and `eval_suite.json` as canonical; note in the submission README that root-level copies are historical/dev artifacts.

## Verification

- `POST /api/store-manager/run` against a shop with seeded demo data (`POST /api/products/seed-demo` or `/api/dashboard/seed-hackathon`) returns all 7 stage results and writes a `DecisionTrace` + at least one `PredictionLog`.
- Confirm the `/predict` route fix: `curl -X POST localhost:5001/api/ml/predict` (with ml-service running on 8000) returns 200, not the current proxy failure.
- Load `client/src/screens/StoreManager.jsx` in the browser (`npm run dev`), click the button, watch the stage-by-stage UI update, confirm no raw Mutagent/ADL terminology leaks into the owner-facing copy.
- Run the two Mutagent `*evaluate` cycles and diff the resulting scorecards — confirm the optimized run's pass rate/metrics genuinely improved on the same dataset (not cherry-picked cases).
- Grep the final `submissions/team-nirvikalp/` folder and copied transcripts for `mongodb+srv://`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `BHASHINI_API_KEY` patterns before pushing.

**Expanded `DecisionTrace` schema** in `server/db.js` (widened per review feedback — this is the AI's memory, not just a log):
`DecisionTrace { shopId, cycleId, stage, goal, decision, reason[] (structured factors: e.g. {factor:"yesterday_sales", value:32}, {factor:"weather", value:"rain_forecast"}, {factor:"day_effect", value:"+18% Sunday demand"}), confidence, expectedOutcome, actualOutcome, financialImpact {estimated, realized}, actionTaken, ownerDecision ("approved"|"overridden"|"pending"), overrideReason, timestamp, linkedPredictionLogId, lessonLearned }`.
`reason[]` is what makes a recommendation explainable ("Order 25 Milk — sold 32 yesterday, rain forecast, Sunday demand +18%, only 5 in stock, confidence 91%") instead of a bare instruction. `lessonLearned` is populated by LEARN (see below) and is what turns raw outcomes into reusable rules, not just numbers.

**Goals, not just observations**: OBSERVE now also loads/sets a small `Goal` list per cycle (`reduce_stockouts`, `increase_profit`, `recover_udhaar`, `reduce_dead_inventory` — start hardcoded with sensible defaults derived from current KPIs, e.g. auto-prioritize `recover_udhaar` if `totalCredit` is high). Every `DecisionTrace` row is tagged with which goal it serves. This is what turns the orchestrator from "automation that reacts to data" into "a manager that pursues objectives" — and gives DIAGNOSE/OPTIMIZE something to optimize *against* (did this decision move the goal or not).

**LEARN produces lessons, not just rows**: after each cycle, a Gemini call compares `expectedOutcome` vs `actualOutcome` for every prior decision and writes a one-line `lessonLearned` back onto the `DecisionTrace` (e.g. "Rain increases milk demand ~40% — raise reorder qty on rain-forecast days"). Aggregate distinct lessons per product/category into a small `shopLessons` collection so future OBSERVE/UNDERSTAND stages can inject "known lessons for this shop" into their prompts — this is the actual self-improvement mechanism, distinct from (and complementary to) the Mutagent `*optimize` step which tunes the orchestrator's code/thresholds.

**Owner approval + override loop** (Mutagent's own "nothing auto-advances, every apply is approval-gated" principle, applied to the runtime): EXECUTE never fires automatically for financially material actions — it produces a pending `DecisionTrace` with `ownerDecision: "pending"`. The owner approves, or overrides with a reason. Overrides get the same LEARN treatment as failed predictions: "owner disagreed, reason: X" becomes a lesson too. This is the human-in-the-loop story judges expect and it doubles as free training signal.

**Simulation mode**: before EXECUTE, run a cheap what-if comparison ("if no reorder: tomorrow stockout, est. loss ₹850" vs "if reorder: est. profit +₹2600") using the same `/predict/stockout` call already available, and attach both branches to the `DecisionTrace` so the owner sees the counterfactual, not just the recommendation.

**New route `server/routes/storeManager.js`**:
- `POST /api/store-manager/run` — executes one full cycle, streams stage progress via SSE/polling with the exact stage list the owner sees (Observing Inventory → Analyzing Sales → Checking Weather → Checking Festival Calendar → Running ML Forecast → Comparing Yesterday → Diagnosing Forecast Error → Generating Purchase Order → Creating CEO Brief → Sending WhatsApp → Done), each stage checked off as it completes.
- `GET /api/store-manager/history` — past cycles/traces.
- `POST /api/store-manager/approve` — approve/override a pending decision (`{decisionId, decision: "approved"|"overridden", reason?}`).
- `GET /api/store-manager/impact` — aggregates the just-completed cycle's `financialImpact.realized` + counts into a single "Today's Impact" summary: `{revenueSaved, stockoutsPrevented, ordersGenerated, udhaarRecovered, avgConfidence, executionTimeMs}` — this is the end-of-cycle scorecard the demo closes on.
- `GET /api/store-manager/explain?query=...` — lightweight Q&A over `DecisionTrace`: owner asks "why did you order milk?", handler finds the matching trace row and returns its `reason[]`/`lessonLearned` directly (retrieval, not a fresh LLM call — traces already contain the explanation, this just surfaces it).

Mount all of these in `server/index.js` alongside existing routers.

# ANTARYA × Mutagent — Autonomous Store Manager Implementation Plan

## Context

HackIndia Spark-11's Mutagent track judges on: (1) most sophisticated agent — real jobs/tools/triggers/integrations, (2) a **closed, self-improving dev loop** (`*build → *evaluate → *diagnose → *optimize`, on repeat), (3) a bonus extension to the ADL system itself, (4) proof via a ≥20-item dataset + passing scorecard, (5) product feedback filed with `mutagent-cli feedback`. Submission requires the PR to `mutagent-io/mutagent-hackathon` under `submissions/team-nirvikalp/`, **plus the actual Claude Code session `.jsonl` transcripts** (main + sub-agents) and all trace files — so the Mutagent ADL work must happen live in Claude Code sessions run from this project, not be written up after the fact.

ANTARYA today has real, working AI modules (Gemini chat/advisor/vision OCR, Bhashini voice, a two-stage hurdle ML service) but they don't coordinate — nothing evaluates whether yesterday's forecast was right, diagnoses why, or improves tomorrow's thresholds. The user's blueprint asks for an "Autonomous Store Manager" that makes Mutagent load-bearing, not decorative.

**Key correction to the user's blueprint**: Mutagent's ADL (`*spec/*build/*evaluate/*diagnose/*optimize`) is a **development-lifecycle tool driven by a coding agent**, not a runtime API you call per HTTP request. The plan below keeps that distinction explicit and makes it the actual selling point:

1. **Runtime layer** (our code) — `Autonomous Store Manager`: a 7-stage orchestration (Observe→Understand→Evaluate→Diagnose→Optimize→Execute→Learn) that runs live when the owner clicks "Start," using ANTARYA's existing Gemini/Bhashini/ML modules as tools. This is the "sophisticated agent, real jobs/tools/triggers" criterion.
2. **Dev-time layer** (Mutagent ADL, run inside Claude Code) — used to *spec, build, evaluate, diagnose, and optimize* the Store Manager's own logic (reorder thresholds, confidence gates, prompts) against a real dataset. This is the "self-evolving loop" criterion.
3. **The connective tissue that makes Mutagent essential, not bolted on** — the Store Manager's LEARN stage writes every decision + its real outcome (predicted vs. actual) into Mongo. That log becomes the **eval dataset** Mutagent judges in `*evaluate`. `*diagnose` explains real failures (not synthetic ones). `*optimize` changes real thresholds/prompts, committed back into the runtime code. Run it twice (baseline cycle → optimize → second cycle) to produce a documented before/after improvement, not a static 100% claim.

This also fixes a currently broken route (`POST /api/ml/predict` proxies to a nonexistent FastAPI `/predict` — only `/predict/demand` and `/predict/stockout` exist) and replaces the fabricated 100% `scorecard.json` with real numbers, per the user's explicit decision.

## Scope decisions (from user)

- **Scorecard**: regenerate honestly from real execution traces. Ship two cycles: baseline pass/fail numbers → diagnose → optimize → second cycle showing measurable improvement on the same dataset. Include business metrics (stockouts prevented, forecast error change, response time, revenue impact) alongside pass/fail.
- **Trigger model**: both — manual "Start Autonomous Store Manager" button for the live demo, plus an optional scheduled early-morning run (`node-cron`) for the "always-on OS" narrative.
- **Round 2 (post-review) additions** — a second pass reviewed this plan and pushed on 10 specific weak points. All ten are incorporated below because they attack the same gap: the original design *records* decisions but doesn't make them *explainable, goal-directed, financially quantified, or contestable by the owner*. Each item below maps to one of those ten points.

## Architecture

### 1. Runtime: Autonomous Store Manager

**New file `server/services/storeManager.js`** — orchestrates the cycle by calling *existing* code, not reimplementing it:

- OBSERVE: reuse `buildShopContext(shopId)` from `server/routes/ai.js` (products/sales/customers/expenses) + `GET /api/dashboard/` KPIs + `GET /api/dashboard/suggestions` + `POST /api/ml/ceo-brief`. Bundle into one structured `StoreContext` object (the current `buildShopContext` returns a prose string for Gemini — add a sibling function returning structured JSON for the orchestrator to reason over programmatically).
- UNDERSTAND: one Gemini call (reuse the model-fallback pattern already in `ai.js`) that turns `StoreContext` into a prioritized list of business problems, not API calls.
- EVALUATE: pull the last cycle's decisions from the new `DecisionTrace` collection, join against `ActualLog` (already tracks `absoluteError`/`percentageError` per `server/routes/learning.js`) to score each prior recommendation pass/fail.
- DIAGNOSE: for each failed prediction, a Gemini call constrained to the specific failure taxonomy in the blueprint (weather, festival, supplier delay, threshold, seasonality) — not generic text.
- OPTIMIZE: propose concrete parameter changes (e.g., adjust `minStock` threshold, safety_stock in the `/ceo-brief` call, confidence cutoff) — stored as a proposal, not silently applied (mirrors Mutagent's own "nothing auto-advances, every apply is approval-gated" principle).
- EXECUTE (only after owner approval or auto-approve toggle): calls existing endpoints — WhatsApp order text generation (already in Dashboard.jsx pattern), `POST /api/learning/log-prediction`, writes a `DecisionTrace` row.
- LEARN: every stage's input/output is appended to `DecisionTrace`; this is what feeds Mutagent's eval dataset later.

**Expanded `DecisionTrace` schema** in `server/db.js` (widened per review feedback — this is the AI's memory, not just a log):
`DecisionTrace { shopId, cycleId, stage, goal, decision, reason[] (structured factors: e.g. {factor:"yesterday_sales", value:32}, {factor:"weather", value:"rain_forecast"}, {factor:"day_effect", value:"+18% Sunday demand"}), confidence, expectedOutcome, actualOutcome, financialImpact {estimated, realized}, actionTaken, ownerDecision ("approved"|"overridden"|"pending"), overrideReason, timestamp, linkedPredictionLogId, lessonLearned }`.
`reason[]` is what makes a recommendation explainable ("Order 25 Milk — sold 32 yesterday, rain forecast, Sunday demand +18%, only 5 in stock, confidence 91%") instead of a bare instruction. `lessonLearned` is populated by LEARN (see below) and is what turns raw outcomes into reusable rules, not just numbers.

This is the human-in-the-loop story judges expect and it doubles as free training signal.

- `GET /api/store-manager/history` — past cycles/traces.
- `POST /api/store-manager/approve` — approve/override a pending decision (`{decisionId, decision: "approved"|"overridden", reason?}`).
- `GET /api/store-manager/impact` — aggregates the just-completed cycle's `financialImpact.realized` + counts into a single "Today's Impact" summary: `{revenueSaved, stockoutsPrevented, ordersGenerated, udhaarRecovered, avgConfidence, executionTimeMs}` — this is the end-of-cycle scorecard the demo closes on.
- `GET /api/store-manager/explain?query=...` — lightweight Q&A over `DecisionTrace`: owner asks "why did you order milk?", handler finds the matching trace row and returns its `reason[]`/`lessonLearned` directly (retrieval, not a fresh LLM call — traces already contain the explanation, this just surfaces it).

Mount all of these in `server/index.js` alongside existing routers.

**Scheduled trigger**: add `node-cron` (or reuse if already a dependency — verify) in `server/index.js` to call the same orchestrator function on an early-morning schedule, writing results for the owner to review on login — same code path as the manual button, just a different trigger.

### 2. Frontend: Autonomous Store Manager screen

New `client/src/screens/StoreManager.jsx` (+ CSS, following existing screen patterns like `LearningEngine.jsx`): a "▶ Start Autonomous Store Manager" button that triggers `POST /api/store-manager/run`, then renders the stage-by-stage checklist narrative (Observing Inventory ✓ → Analyzing Sales ✓ → Checking Weather ✓ → Checking Festival Calendar ✓ → Running ML Forecast ✓ → Comparing Yesterday ✓ → Diagnosing Forecast Error ✓ → Generating Purchase Order ✓ → Creating CEO Brief ✓ → Sending WhatsApp ✓ → Done) as each stage event arrives — no Mutagent terminology exposed to the shop owner. Each generated recommendation renders with its `reason[]` inline ("Order 25 Milk — sold 32 yesterday, rain forecast, +18% Sunday demand, confidence 91%") plus Approve/Override buttons wired to `POST /api/store-manager/approve`. On completion, fetch `GET /api/store-manager/impact` and render a closing "Today's Impact" card (revenue saved, stockouts prevented, orders generated, udhaar recovered, confidence, execution time) — this is the moment the dashboard visibly updates and is the actual demo payoff. Add a small "Ask why" input on this screen and on `Dashboard.jsx` that hits `GET /api/store-manager/explain` so the owner can query past decisions directly. Add nav entry alongside existing screens.

### 3. Dev-time: Mutagent ADL loop (run inside Claude Code, produces submission artifacts)

Executed as actual Claude Code sessions from this project directory (required so `.jsonl` transcripts exist for submission):

1. `*spec` — author/refine `submissions/team-nirvikalp/agentspec.yaml` to describe the Autonomous Store Manager specifically (not the whole app) — capabilities: `observe_business_context`, `evaluate_past_decisions`, `diagnose_failure`, `optimize_thresholds`, `execute_actions`, `learn_from_outcomes`.

7. File feedback throughout via `mutagent-cli feedback "..."` as real friction is hit (not retrofitted).

Use `Skill(mutagent-cli)` for exact command syntax rather than guessing — it's already installed per `.mutagentrc.json` (workspace `0262ac0d-b8cc-4b0a-a568-148db0bbb597`).

HackIndia Spark-11's Mutagent track judges on: (1) most sophisticated agent — real jobs/tools/triggers/integrations, (2) a **closed, self-improving dev loop** (`*build → *evaluate → *diagnose → *optimize`, on repeat), (3) a bonus extension to the ADL system itself, (4) proof via a ≥20-item dataset + passing scorecard, (5) product feedback filed with `mutagent-cli feedback`. Submission requires the PR to `mutagent-io/mutagent-hackathon` under `submissions/team-nirvikalp/`, **plus the actual Claude Code session `.jsonl` transcripts** (main + sub-agents) and all trace files — so the Mutagent ADL work must happen live in Claude Code sessions run from this project, not be written up after the fact.

ANTARYA today has real, working AI modules (Gemini chat/advisor/vision OCR, Bhashini voice, a two-stage hurdle ML service) but they don't coordinate — nothing evaluates whether yesterday's forecast was right, diagnoses why, or improves tomorrow's thresholds. The user's blueprint asks for an "Autonomous Store Manager" that makes Mutagent load-bearing, not decorative.

**Key correction to the user's blueprint**: Mutagent's ADL (`*spec/*build/*evaluate/*diagnose/*optimize`) is a **development-lifecycle tool driven by a coding agent**, not a runtime API you call per HTTP request. The plan below keeps that distinction explicit and makes it the actual selling point:

1. **Runtime layer** (our code) — `Autonomous Store Manager`: a 7-stage orchestration (Observe→Understand→Evaluate→Diagnose→Optimize→Execute→Learn) that runs live when the owner clicks "Start," using ANTARYA's existing Gemini/Bhashini/ML modules as tools. This is the "sophisticated agent, real jobs/tools/triggers" criterion.
2. **Dev-time layer** (Mutagent ADL, run inside Claude Code) — used to *spec, build, evaluate, diagnose, and optimize* the Store Manager's own logic (reorder thresholds, confidence gates, prompts) against a real dataset. This is the "self-evolving loop" criterion.
3. **The connective tissue that makes Mutagent essential, not bolted on** — the Store Manager's LEARN stage writes every decision + its real outcome (predicted vs. actual) into Mongo. That log becomes the **eval dataset** Mutagent judges in `*evaluate`. `*diagnose` explains real failures (not synthetic ones). `*optimize` changes real thresholds/prompts, committed back into the runtime code. Run it twice (baseline cycle → optimize → second cycle) to produce a documented before/after improvement, not a static 100% claim.

This also fixes a currently broken route (`POST /api/ml/predict` proxies to a nonexistent FastAPI `/predict` — only `/predict/demand` and `/predict/stockout` exist) and replaces the fabricated 100% `scorecard.json` with real numbers, per the user's explicit decision.

- **Trigger model**: both — manual "Start Autonomous Store Manager" button for the live demo, plus an optional scheduled early-morning run (`node-cron`) for the "always-on OS" narrative.

Bundle into one structured `StoreContext` object (the current `buildShopContext` returns a prose string for Gemini — add a sibling function returning structured JSON for the orchestrator to reason over programmatically).
- UNDERSTAND: one Gemini call (reuse the model-fallback pattern already in `ai.js`) that turns `StoreContext` into a prioritized list of business problems, not API calls.
- EVALUATE: pull the last cycle's decisions from the new `DecisionTrace` collection, join against `ActualLog` (already tracks `absoluteError`/`percentageError` per `server/routes/learning.js`) to score each prior recommendation pass/fail.

- mutagent-agentspec: The ADL ① SPEC stage: a guided requirements interview that captures WHAT an AI agent IS and emits
a portable, validated agentspec.yaml. The spec is the Definition (the interface — persona, the
actual system prompt, jobs-to-be-done, context sources, tools across four buckets, agent type,
inbound activation triggers, decision modeling, standard operating procedures, and binary
eval criteria). BUILD is owned by mutagent-builder, which consumes the validated spec and implements
it into a target framework or harness. First invocation: auto-detects install. Then *spec runs a parent-session
interview (AskUserQuestion on Claude Code, chat multi-choice fallback elsewhere) → emits + validates
agentspec.yaml; *validate-spec is the TypeBox round-trip schema gate. The target may be a framework
(mastra / deepagents / pydantic-ai / langgraph) OR a harness (harness:claude-code / harness:codex).
After *spec or *validate-spec succeeds, Helix suggests *build; *build is owned by mutagent-builder.
- mutagent-builder: The ADL ② BUILD stage: implements a validated agentspec.yaml into a target framework or harness.
Owns *build + the two agents (ai-engineer Actor · ai-architect Verifier); *build dispatches them
through a TDD + coverage loop. The *sync-spec COMMAND is owned by mutagent-agentspec — builder
provides the ai-architect #sync-spec MODE (the single implementation-reader) that agentspec's
*sync-spec delegates to (Helix-mediated), and that *build reuses build-internally when code drifted
ahead. ai-engineer applies any resulting gated spec writes.
- mutagent-diagnostics: The DIAGNOSE stage of the agentic development lifecycle (ADL ④, feeding ⑤ OPTIMIZE).
Finds out why an agent misbehaves and gets approved fixes applied: it reads
evidence from the agent's real traces and user feedback, pins down root causes,
ranks candidate remedies in a reviewable report, and — only after your approval —
applies the chosen fixes safely, via PR for local agents or REST for cloud ones.
Covers traces from Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, local JSONL, and Claude Code or Codex
sessions; fixes agents defined as coding-agent markdown (Claude, Codex, Cursor,
OpenCode), as code (Mastra, Cloud Agent SDK), or on a cloud platform — or runs
report-only when nothing should change. Pick it when the ask is to diagnose,
root-cause, or fix agent behavior.
- mutagent-evaluator: The EVALUATE stage of the agentic development lifecycle (ADL ③). Builds and runs
trustworthy evaluations for AI agents and skills: from a subject's real traces it
learns what success and failure look like, turns that into binary eval criteria,
and scores the subject to a clear gate verdict. It only judges — failures route to
mutagent-diagnostics, never fixed here. Pick it whenever the ask is to evaluate,
judge, score, or build and validate evals for an agent or skill: any plain
"evaluate this" runs *evaluate — one judge per trajectory walks the evidence
layers (code checks → outcome → trajectory → tool outputs → context), criteria
binding evidence across all of them; the *evaluate-[layer] variants scope the same
pipeline to one layer; *discover mines new criteria, never re-recommending one it
has; *audit is a separate, explicit-only static auditor, never the fallback for a
plain evaluate. Also the verifier inside mutagent-skill-builder's SIMULATE.
- mutagent-helix: Helix — the MutagenT Agentic Development Lifecycle (ADL) conductor. Drives a skill or agent
through the full lifecycle — spec → build → evaluate → diagnose → optimize — by sequencing a set
of standalone lifecycle-stage skills and adjudicating the gates between them. Helix is a
natural-language *command router: it indexes the system, tracks where you are in the loop, hands
each stage to its owning skill, and keeps every apply (a code change, a platform update)
approval-gated. First invocation auto-detects setup and guides onboarding; subsequent
invocations render the ADL dashboard and await a *command (or free text, which routes through the
intent layer). Ships the lifecycle-stage skills it conducts: mutagent-agentspec (① SPEC — a
guided interview that emits a portable agentspec.yaml), mutagent-builder (② BUILD — implement the
validated spec into the target framework/harness), mutagent-evaluator (③ EVALUATE — mine criteria
from traces, judge, validate the judge, build datasets; judge only, never fixes), and
mutagent-diagnostics (④ DIAGNOSE — RCA + ranked remedies from real traces). The ⑤ OPTIMIZE stage
routes to mutagent-optimize (bundled inside the @mutagent/helix package, not a standalone release) — the session-conducted,
bounded eval-driven optimize loop (Build → Eval → Diagnose → Optimize ↻) whose one apply-gate at
convergence goes through the shared `mutagent-cli apply`. Helix never executes a stage's inner
work — it routes. Two invariants hold the loop
together: judge-never-fix (the evaluator decides; fai…
- mutagent-optimize: The ADL ⑤ OPTIMIZE stage: the closed, bounded, eval-driven optimize loop
(Build → Eval → Diagnose → Optimize ↻). ONE command *optimize runs a confirm-once
→ bounded auto-loop → one apply-gate at convergence. A sub-orchestration skill in
the shape of evaluator/diagnostics: the parent session owns the loop FSM + gates
and dispatches a BORROWED crew it does not itself execute — ai-engineer (WRITE),
ai-architect (VERIFY), evaluator (JUDGE, re-eval), diagnostics-analyzer (RCA).
optimize writes NOTHING itself: the WRITE delegates to ② builder, the JUDGE to
③ evaluator, the RCA to ④ diagnostics, and the TRANSPORT to `mutagent-cli apply`
(a call OUT to the shared service, NOT a subcommand). Absorbs the retired
diagnostics apply-worker's target mechanics via that shared apply layer.
- mutagent-ship: The ADL ⑥ SHIP stage: the gated stage taking a GATE-passed subject from
evaluated → shipped. Three verbs in order — merge → monitor → watch. For the
code / pull-request MVP target: MERGE a GitHub PR (standardized changelog +
ship-manifest), MONITOR CI to green (bounded mechanical refinement), then WATCH
the deployed agent's traces for regression — recommending an evidence-linked
rollback, never performing one. Operator-only (INV-SHIP-1): no trigger, chain,
agent, or script may launch *ship. Apply ≠ deploy (INV-SHIP-2): the spine stops
at the operator merge gate; nothing deploys as a side effect. FULL STAGE
(P1–P4): entry gate → ship-manifest → PR → merge gate (P1) · CI-green monitor
FSM + bounded refinement (P2) · post-deploy watch + rollback recommendation +
revert-PR path + DIAGNOSE handoff + ship-report (P3) · the run-scoped
ship-monitor agent (P4). Decision/render cores are pure + tested; live CI
polling, the fix actor's push, and trace acquisition are agent ops.

Runtime layer is built, verified against real data, and committed. Here's where things stand.

## What's working (verified, not claimed)

**The Autonomous Store Manager** — one cycle coordinating your existing Gemini/Bhashini/ML modules:

- 12 stages stream live to the UI via SSE (Observing Inventory → … → Learning From Outcomes), ran in ~1.6s
- Every recommendation carries structured reasoning + confidence + a counterfactual: *"Order 25 Milk — sold 32 last week, only 5 left, monsoon, Raksha Bandhan in 12 days, 80% sure"* alongside "if you don't: stockout in 2 days, −₹850 / if you do: +₹2600"
- Goals (`reduce_stockouts`, `recover_udhaar`, `reduce_dead_inventory`, `increase_profit`) derived from actual KPIs, and every decision is tagged with which one it serves
- Owner approves or overrides with a reason; nothing material fires automatically
- Overrides become lessons — I confirmed the round trip: override → lesson stored → injected into the next cycle's reasoning context
- "Ask why" answers from stored traces, not a fresh LLM call

**Two real bugs fixed along the way:**
1. `POST /api/ml/predict` proxied to a FastAPI route that doesn't exist (`/predict` — only `/predict/demand` and `/predict/stockout` do). It was broken for everyone.
2. Bigger one: the cycle wrote predictions but nothing ever wrote the matching actuals, so EVALUATE/DIAGNOSE/OPTIMIZE would have returned empty forever — the self-improving half was inert. Now reconciled from real sale line items, plus a walk-forward backtest. It currently scores **39 real pairs at a 21% pass rate**, which produced 31 diagnoses and 31 optimization proposals.

I also kept the impact card honest: "Approve Kiya (anumaan)" is separated from confirmed value, with a note saying the real outcome gets checked in 7 days. Approving no longer silently relabels an estimate as realized.

## Two things you should know

**Your existing `scorecard.json` was already honest** — 45% from real runs. The "100%" only ever existed in the blueprint prose, so there's nothing fabricated to walk back.

**Helix is now installed** (7 ADL skills), but `mutagent usage` shows **0 LLM providers configured**. That likely gates `*evaluate`/`*optimize`. Worth sorting before starting the loop rather than hitting it at stage 4.

## What's next, and one thing I won't fake

The ADL loop (`*spec` → sync the existing implementation → `*evaluate` → `*diagnose` → `*optimize` → re-evaluate) is what generates your required session transcripts. Important: **I hand-wrote `storeManager.js`** — the transcripts will show that plainly. So we should run `*spec` and bring the existing code under it via sync-spec, and say so in the submission README. Claiming `*build` wrote it would be contradicted by the very artifacts judges replay.

Also note your branch tracks `target_repo` → `Arjundas08/antarya3`, not `origin`. The submission PR goes to a fork of `mutagent-io/mutagent-hackathon` — I haven't pushed anything anywhere.

Want me to start the ADL loop with `*spec`, or sort the provider key first?

- ai-architect: Pure subagent reviewer — the *build VERIFIER + the SINGLE implementation-reader. NEVER writes or edits source — read-only review only.
 (Tools: Read, Bash, SendMessage)

- ai-engineer: Pure subagent executor — the *build ACTOR. Receives a validated agentspec.yaml + a chosen target (framework or harness). Crawls the pinned Appendix framework docs FRESH (WebFetch) at build time, plans the target repo hierarchy per framework conventions (dogfood H6), scaffolds the implementation in the target, and runs a TDD verify loop (test-first → lint → typecheck → build → test). Emits a scaffolded implementation + a build report. Worktree-isolated. ALSO the fix ACTOR for the ADL ③ OPTIMIZE / EDD loop (F18): consumes an EddChangeRequest the evaluator (judge-only) sends over SendMessage, amends the named Agent/AgentSpec target (def→impl cascade on an `agentspec` target), and replies with a ChangeRequestResponse for re-eval.

Ships ZERO subject-specific logic; operates on a generated SUBJECT PROFILE (subjects/<name>/{eval-matrix,behavior-tree,methodology-review}.yaml). Audits any skill/agent against its profile and emits a 4-tab master-audit report (eval-matrix · data-leak · variance · methodology). On-demand, advisory, operator-out-of-loop.
 (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Monitor, SendMessage)

- dataset-builder: Pure subagent executor. Receives a subject's DIMENSIONS (axes of variation) + the user-confirmed SEED tuples + a target count. Generates additional dimension tuples, converts EACH to a realistic natural-language query (a SEPARATE step from tuple generation), and self-filters for quality (realism + non-redundancy). Emits a structured candidate-cases file to the run scratchpad; the parent's `scripts/build-dataset.ts` AGGREGATEs it (cartesian/dedup/near-dup/id). Reasons on the HOST runtime (NO provider key). GENERATOR, never a judge — never runs the subject, never decides pass/fail. Time cap 240s.
 (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Monitor, SendMessage)

- diagnostics-analyzer: Pure subagent executor. Receives a trace slice (list of trace IDs + scope context). Runs CODE-FIRST tiered analysis (pattern-match → tree-match → structural → LLM for deviations only). Emits structured + freeform findings to orchestrator scratchpad + per-file. Time cap 240s.
 (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Monitor, SendMessage)

- discovery: Pure subagent executor — trace collection cell. Receives a HandoverBundle carrying a TraceQuery (kind:config ArtifactRef). Sizes the window via `mutagent-cli trace count`, then collects and normalizes → UniTF JSONL + TraceManifest via `mutagent-cli trace fetch --export`. Emits a HandoverBundle whose inputs[] are the trace JSONL + the manifest, ready for Diagnostics or Evaluator to consume. No analysis — collection only.
 (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Monitor, SendMessage)

- dogfood-monitor: Background session-tail cell for the hidden `*dogfood` command. Receives { sessionId?, source_dir, runId }. Resolves the latest session in the dogfood TARGET project's Claude-projects dir (NOT the build project), discovers its dispatched subagent JSONLs, and arms a persistent Monitor on all of them. On drift (a new *command / ADL stage / [feedback] block / subagent) OR every 3 minutes it reconstructs the trajectory, extracts feedback, and re-renders a live status HTML — auto-opened — while appending the absorbed feedback ledger. Terminates on *dogfood-stop or session inactivity. Observe-only: never edits the target.
 (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Monitor, SendMessage)

- evaluator: Pure subagent executor — the unified eval-DEVELOPMENT cell. ONE agent, two modes: discover (mine emergent BINARY ACTIONABLE criteria from a trace batch) + judge (score against criteria). Judge has two fan-out axes: trajectory (one judge scores the WHOLE matrix for one session — the headline path) and criterion (one judge per criterion across a trace-slice). Critique-before-verdict, binary (not Likert), inaction-can-be-success, judge-only (EV-051 — never fixes). Reasons on the HOST runtime (Claude Code) — NO external provider key. Pinned model + temperature 0 (C-PIN). Dispatched by the parent, MASS-PARALLEL.
 (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Monitor, SendMessage)

- monitor: Background watch cell for the hidden `*monitor` command — the EXTERNAL (outward) monitor. Receives { runId }. Arms a persistent watch on the DORMANT `config.triggers` (evaluate/diagnose rules). On an incoming system event (trace-count · schedule · ci · manual) it evaluates the rules (scripts/monitor/triggers.ts). On a match it emits a HandoverBundle to the target ADL stage (via the orchestrator dispatch model, same as `*discover`) AND posts a discrete Slack NOTIFICATION (scripts/monitor/slack-notify.ts). Ships DISABLED — no auto-fire until triggers.<stage>.enabled:true. Terminates on *monitor-stop. Observe-and-route only: never edits a target; never runs a stage itself.
 (Tools: Read, Bash, Monitor, SendMessage)

- ship-monitor: Run-scoped background observe+recommend cell for the ⑥ SHIP stage — a SIBLING of the general `monitor` (reuses the same event-bus multiplexer + `ci`/`trace-count` lanes, but armed by ONE *ship and terminating at watch-window close, NEVER an always-on watch). Receives { shipId, pr, manifestPath }. Arms a Monitor-driven CI watch on `gh pr checks` (ci lane; classify red → RefinementRequest to the parent, bounded + mechanical-only), then — on deploy-confirm (merge for direct-load, installed-confirmed for installed-copy) — runs the post-deploy source-platform trace watch (mutagent-cli trace, legal acquisition paths) against the pre-ship baseline. On regression emits an evidence-linked rollback RECOMMENDATION (trace refs) — NEVER rolls back, merges, or pushes. Terminates when the watch window closes (≤30m, KP-6), on escalation, or on abort.
 (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Monitor, SendMessage)
